authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: White Mountains agreed to sell 5.5 million MediaAlpha shares at $13.90 per share. The filing does not say the sale has closed.
WTM Partners made two acquisitions, Basesix and Hawkeye Electric, which helped drive its revenue and earnings growth.
White Mountains repurchased and retired 103,827 common shares for $217 million in the first nine months of 2026.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description.
business_model.claim: White Mountains is a holding company that buys, runs and eventually sells businesses and assets in insurance, financial services and related sectors. Its earnings come from the operating subsidiaries and from investment results.
quotes: White Mountains is engaged in the business of making opportunistic and value-oriented acquisitions of businesses and assets in the insurance, financial services and related sectors, operating these businesses and assets through its subsidiaries and, if and when attractive exit valuations become available, disposing of these businesses and assets.

business_model.basis: Segment names are stated in the 10-K and appear as segment captions in the 10-Q statements; treating WTM Partners as a segment is inferred from the 10-Q segment captions.
business_model.claim: The company reports through operating segments plus a residual group. The 10-K names Ark/WM Outrigger (P&C insurance and reinsurance), HG Global (municipal bond guarantee reinsurance), Kudu (capital solutions for asset managers) and Distinguished (specialty insurance distribution), with everything else in Other Operations. The 2026 quarterly statements also show a Services, Industrial and Consumer segment (WTM Partners).
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, White Mountains’s reportable segments were Ark/WM Outrigger, HG Global, Kudu and Distinguished, with its remaining operating businesses, holding companies and other assets included in Other Operations.

business_model.basis: Product and channel are stated in the 10-K; the revenue share is read from the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Ark/WM Outrigger is the largest revenue source. It sells specialty property and casualty insurance and reinsurance through brokers, wholesalers and MGAs, and earns premiums plus investment income. Its nine-month segment revenue was a large share of the consolidated total.
quotes: In both jurisdictions, Ark underwrites business primarily through insurance and reinsurance brokers and wholesalers, both in the open market and through managing general agents (“MGAs”).
Ark derives substantially all of its revenues from earned premiums, investment income and net realized and unrealized investment gains (losses).

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and in the 10-K business description of the combined ratio.
business_model.claim: Ark's profit depends on its combined ratio, which is driven by catastrophe losses, prior-year reserve development and underwriting expenses. In the latest quarter and nine months the ratios were 75% and 83%, with catastrophe losses driven mainly by the war in Iran and favorable prior-year development in property and specialty.
quotes: Ark’s combined ratio was 75% and 83% in the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 compared to 76% and 84% in the third quarter and first nine months of 2025.

business_model.basis: Figures are stated in the 10-Q income statement; the mechanism is stated in the 10-K MD&A for 2025 and is applied here to 2026 by inference.
business_model.claim: Ark's costs are claims, acquisition costs and general expenses, plus a non-operating charge for contingent consideration. That charge rises with growth in Ark's tangible book value.
quotes: The increase in the contingent consideration liability was driven primarily by strong growth in Ark’s tangible book value in the year.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A; cyclicality is also stated in the 10-K risk factors.
business_model.claim: Ark's volume is shaped by the property market cycle. Nine-month gross written premiums fell because of softening property pricing, partly offset by growth in specialty, casualty and accident & health.
quotes: The decrease in gross written premiums in the first nine months of 2026 was driven primarily by reduced writings in property as a result of the softening market conditions, partially offset by growth in the specialty, casualty and accident & health lines of business.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and the 10-Q statements and MD&A.
business_model.claim: HG Global earns money by reinsuring municipal bond insurance written by BAM, its only customer. Revenue comes from earned premiums, investment income and interest on BAM Surplus Notes, and is swung by the fair value of those notes and of the bond portfolio.
quotes: HG Re is only licensed to provide reinsurance to BAM.

Our reinsurance subsidiary, HG Re, provides (i) first-loss reinsurance protection of up to 15%-of-par outstanding for each policy assumed from BAM and (ii) last-dollar protection for exposures on municipal bonds insured by BAM in excess of the NYDFS single issuer limits.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and the 10-Q MD&A and income statement.
business_model.claim: Kudu provides capital to asset and wealth managers through Participation Contracts. Its results come from net investment income plus fair-value gains or losses on those contracts, so higher discount rates cut revenue in the latest quarter.
quotes: Kudu provides capital solutions for asset and wealth management firms through Participation Contracts.

The decrease in net realized and unrealized investment gains in the third quarter of 2026 was driven by a decrease in the fair value of Kudu’s Participation Contracts, primarily due to the impact of higher discount rates, partially offset by growth in assets under management at several managers.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and the 10-Q MD&A; the nine-month operating-loss reading is stated by the company.
business_model.claim: Distinguished is a managing general agent and program administrator. It earns commissions on premiums that carriers charge insureds, while the carriers bear the insurance risk. It reported pre-tax losses in the latest quarter and nine months and depends on a few carriers.
quotes: Distinguished generates most of its revenues from commissions that are a portion of premiums charged by insurance companies to their insureds.
Distinguished placed approximately 22% of its business with its single largest carrier during the year ended December 31, 2025.

business_model.basis: Revenue and drivers are stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the link between acquisitions and goodwill is inferred from the balance sheet.
business_model.claim: WTM Partners sells products and services (electrical contracting at Enterprise Solutions and acquired businesses). Its revenue and costs rose sharply in 2026 with organic growth and acquisitions.
quotes: The increases were driven by organic growth at Enterprise Solutions and the acquisitions of Basesix and Hawkeye Electric in the second quarter of 2026.

business_model.basis: Figures are stated in the 10-Q income statement; the explanation is stated in the MD&A.
business_model.claim: Investment results are a major swing factor in reported earnings. Net investment income rose in the latest quarter, but unrealized losses (higher interest rates and a MediaAlpha share price decline) turned the quarter to a loss.
quotes: Results in the third quarter were impacted by higher interest rates and a decline in the MediaAlpha share price, which led to unrealized losses that offset an otherwise solid quarter for operating results.

business_model.basis: Read directly from the 10-Q income statement lines; the cost-driver framing is inferred from the line items.
business_model.claim: Consolidated costs combine insurance claims and acquisition costs, broker commissions, cost of sales for product businesses, contingent-consideration changes and interest. Cost of sales rose faster than product and service revenues grew as the product businesses expanded.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A and the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Portfolio recycling is part of the model. In December 2025 the company sold a controlling interest in the Bamboo Group, so Bamboo no longer contributes revenue, and in 2026 it recorded a small further gain on sale.
quotes: On December 5, 2025, White Mountains completed the sale of a controlling financial interest in the Bamboo Group to affiliates of funds advised by CVC.

business_model.basis: Figures are stated in the 10-Q statements; the funding link is inferred.
business_model.claim: The company returns and redeploys capital by repurchasing its own shares, funded in part by borrowing. It holds undeployed capital for new acquisitions or investments.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, White Mountains’s undeployed capital is roughly $0.8 billion.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K and the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Part of the consolidated profit belongs to minority holders in the operating subsidiaries, notably Ark, so shareholder earnings are below total net income.
quotes: White Mountains owned 72.1% of Ark on a basic shares outstanding basis (61.9% after taking account of management’s equity incentives)

competitive_position.claim: White Mountains describes itself as an opportunistic acquirer and operator of insurance and financial-services businesses. It is a diversified holding company, not a single-line insurer, and its edge comes from capital allocation across segments.
quotes: White Mountains is engaged in the business of making opportunistic and value-oriented acquisitions of businesses and assets in the insurance, financial services and related sectors

competitive_position.claim: Ark, the largest segment, shows strong underwriting results. Its combined ratio was 75% in Q3 2026 and 83% for nine months, against 76% and 84% a year earlier.
quotes: Ark’s combined ratio was 75% and 83% in the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 compared to 76% and 84% in the third quarter and first nine months of 2025.

competitive_position.claim: Ark's scale was $2,557 million of gross written premiums in 2025, up from $2,207 million in 2024. It underwrites through Lloyd's syndicates and a Bermuda company.
quotes: Ark reported gross written premiums of $2,557 million

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the 10-K risk factors
competitive_position.claim: Softening property markets are a named threat to Ark's volume. Nine-month gross written premiums fell to $2,254 million from $2,289 million because Ark reduced property writings.
quotes: reduced writings in property as a result of the softening market conditions

competitive_position.claim: Ark's larger competitors are named as a threat. The 10-K says many have greater financial resources, deeper broker relationships and possibly higher ratings.
quotes: Many of these competitors have greater financial resources, have more established long-term and continuing business relationships throughout the insurance and reinsurance industries and may have higher financial strength ratings, which can represent significant competitive advantages for them.

competitive_position.claim: Ark's financial strength rating underpins its competitive position, and a downgrade is a named threat.
quotes: The maintenance of an “A-” or better financial strength rating is particularly important to Ark’s ability to write property and casualty insurance and reinsurance business in most markets.

competitive_position.claim: Ark has ongoing exposure to the war in Iran through its specialty and marine & energy lines. It recorded estimated losses of $10 million in Q3 and $52 million for nine months.
quotes: Ark has ongoing exposure to the war in Iran, primarily through the specialty and marine & energy lines of business.

competitive_position.claim: HG Global's position depends on one counterparty. HG Re is licensed only to reinsure BAM, and BAM's rating and competition from Assured are named threats.
quotes: HG Re is only licensed to provide reinsurance to BAM.
BAM’s primary competitor is Assured, which also provides financial guarantees on non-municipal debt, including structured finance.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release
competitive_position.claim: HG Global's recent results were weak on valuation. The BAM Surplus Notes fair value fell to $336 million from $353 million in Q3 2026, driven by higher interest rates on the discount rate.
quotes: The fair value of the BAM Surplus Notes decreased to $336 million as of September 30, 2026 compared to $353 million as of June 30, 2026.

competitive_position.claim: Distinguished is growing in volume, with managed premiums up 20% in Q3 2026 and 14% for nine months. It is not yet profitable at the pre-tax level.
quotes: Distinguished’s managed premiums increased 20% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025 and 14% in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the first nine months of 2025.

competitive_position.claim: Distinguished depends on a few carriers, a named threat. About 22% of its business went to its largest carrier and about 61% to its three largest in 2025.
quotes: Distinguished placed approximately 22% of its business with its single largest carrier during the year ended December 31, 2025.

competitive_position.claim: Kudu has a sizable platform in asset-manager capital solutions, but its marks are sensitive to rates. It had deployed $1.2 billion into 32 firms, and its Q3 2026 pre-tax result was a loss.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, Kudu had deployed a total of $1.2 billion, including transaction costs, into 32 asset and wealth management firms globally, including three that have been exited.

competitive_position.claim: Kudu's managers face named industry threats, including a shift to passive investing, fee compression and key-person reliance.
quotes: changes in investor preference from the actively-managed investments offered by Kudu’s managers to passively-managed investments

competitive_position.claim: WTM Partners is growing quickly from a small base. Q3 2026 revenue was $107 million against $54 million a year earlier, driven by organic growth and acquisitions.
quotes: The increases were driven by organic growth at Enterprise Solutions and the acquisitions of Basesix and Hawkeye Electric in the second quarter of 2026.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the earnings release and the 10-Q MD&A
competitive_position.claim: Book value per share fell 1% in Q3 2026. The MediaAlpha holding and higher interest rates produced the unrealized losses, so the investment portfolio is a threat to book value.
quotes: MediaAlpha's share price declined 24% in the quarter, producing $54 million of mark-to-market losses for our remaining position.

competitive_position.claim: Undeployed capital of roughly $0.8 billion supports further acquisitions.
quotes: Undeployed capital remains at roughly $0.8 billion.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement. Assigning the two-value rows to the nine-month columns is inferred from column placement.
financial_health.claim: Cash on hand is modest and fell over the nine months: the balance was 167,400,000 at 30 September 2026 against 185,600,000 at the start of the year, a net change in cash of (18,200,000).

financial_health.basis: Balance sheet figures are stated. That Other Operations includes the parent is from the 10-K business description (P1) and is not shown in the cited items F1 and P4.
financial_health.claim: Holding-company liquid resources shrank: Other Operations short-term investments fell to 236,800,000 from 806,900,000, while management states undeployed capital is roughly $0.8 billion.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, White Mountains’s undeployed capital is roughly $0.8 billion.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the consolidated balance sheet.
financial_health.claim: Consolidated debt rose to 928,600,000 from 837,000,000.0 at year-end 2025, against common shareholders' equity of 5,353,100,000 and total equity of 6,094,800,000.

financial_health.basis: Segment debt figures are stated. The parent-versus-subsidiary reading is inferred from the segment layout and the P1 description of Other Operations.
financial_health.claim: Debt sits mainly in operating subsidiaries, not at the parent: Kudu has 350,900,000, HG Global 197,400,000, Ark 159,000,000.0, Distinguished 140,900,000, WTM Partners 63,100,000 and Other Operations only 17,300,000.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow and income statements. Column assignment inferred from placement.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow was 331,600,000 in the first nine months of 2026, down from 496,600,000, in line with lower net income of 175,300,000 against 388,100,000.

financial_health.basis: Line items are stated. The float interpretation is inferred; the caveat figure (31,600,000) is from the same statement but is not in this claim's numbers.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow exceeds net income largely because of insurance float, not earnings alone: unearned premiums rose 415,900,000 and loss reserves 266,400,000, partly offset by growth in premiums receivable of (382,400,000) and reinsurance recoverables of (240,000,000.0).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement; the funding link is inferred. The figures 885,800,000 and 163,100,000 are from the same statement but are not in this claim's numbers.
financial_health.claim: Cash was used mainly for buybacks and acquisitions: share repurchases of (216,800,000), purchases of consolidated subsidiaries of (179,300,000) and dividends of only (2,400,000); net investing was (192,700,000) and net financing (157,100,000).

financial_health.basis: Flows and balances are stated. The link to acquisitions is inferred from the goodwill increase at WTM Partners and P4's mention of acquisitions.
financial_health.claim: Borrowing is active rather than being run down: in the nine months the company drew 260,900,000 of debt and repaid (169,800,000), paid interest of (51,400,000), and debt grew at HG Global to 197,400,000 from 147,800,000 and at WTM Partners to 63,100,000 from 19,400,000.

financial_health.basis: Balance and expense are stated. The link between the liability and the share-earning mechanism is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Ark carries a contingent consideration liability of 400,000,000.0, up from 328,300,000, with a fair value charge of 71,700,000 in the nine months; the evidence indicates it may be settled in part through additional Ark shares, and the timing and form of settlement are not stated.
quotes: In the future, management rollover shareholders could earn additional shares in Ark if and to the extent that White Mountains achieves certain thresholds for its multiple of invested capital return.

growth_thesis.claim: Ark's underwriting profitability is the main operating engine. Its combined ratio was 75% in the third quarter and 83% for nine months of 2026, against 76% and 84% a year earlier. Ark's tangible book value rose 12% over nine months. For this to continue, underwriting margins must stay well under 100%.
quotes: Ark’s combined ratio was 75% and 83% in the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 compared to 76% and 84% in the third quarter and first nine months of 2025.
Ark reported tangible book value of $1,825 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase of 5% in the third quarter of 2026 and 12% in the first nine months of 2026, including dividends.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the condition is inferred from the combined-ratio components.
growth_thesis.claim: Ark's low combined ratio depends on catastrophe losses and reserve development staying benign. Catastrophe losses in 2026 were driven primarily by the war in Iran, with estimated losses of $10 million in the quarter and $52 million for nine months, and exposure is ongoing.
quotes: Ark has ongoing exposure to the war in Iran, primarily through the specialty and marine & energy lines of business.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the continuation condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Ark's premium growth is mixed. Third-quarter gross written premiums were $386 million against $366 million. Nine-month gross written premiums were $2,254 million against $2,289 million, because softening property markets reduced writings. Growth continuing requires specialty, casualty and accident & health to keep offsetting weaker property.
quotes: The decrease in gross written premiums in the first nine months of 2026 was driven primarily by reduced writings in property as a result of the softening market conditions, partially offset by growth in the specialty, casualty and accident & health lines of business.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the conditions are inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Kudu, the asset-management capital business, keeps growing its base. It deployed $36 million into two new firms in 2026 and now has 32 firms with about $166 billion of combined assets under management. Nine-month adjusted EBITDA was $50 million against $47 million. Continuation requires fair values to hold up as discount rates and the managers' assets under management move.
quotes: Kudu deployed a total of $36 million, including transaction costs, into two new asset management firms in 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the conditions are inferred and the carrier concentration comes from the 10-K risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Distinguished is growing premiums placed but is not yet profitable. Managed premiums rose 20% in the third quarter and 14% for nine months. Pre-tax losses were $13 million and $41 million, and ScaleCo adjusted EBITDA was $5 million and $22 million. Continuation requires carrier and broker relationships to hold and losses to narrow.
quotes: Distinguished’s managed premiums increased 20% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025 and 14% in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the first nine months of 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the balance sheet effects are shown in the F1 segment rows.
growth_thesis.claim: WTM Partners, the services and industrial platform, is growing quickly through organic growth and acquisitions. Total revenues were $107 million in the quarter and $243 million for nine months, against $54 million and $97 million a year earlier. Continuation requires further acquisitions or organic growth at the operating businesses.
quotes: The increases were driven by organic growth at Enterprise Solutions and the acquisitions of Basesix and Hawkeye Electric in the second quarter of 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures stated in the statements; the continuation condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Net investment income is a steady contributor. Consolidated net investment income was 70,600,000 in the third quarter against 59,200,000, and 212,900,000 for nine months against 180,200,000. Continuation requires invested assets and yields to hold up, with fixed income losses from higher rates not swamping it.
quotes: Excluding MediaAlpha, the total consolidated portfolio return on invested assets was flat in the third quarter of 2026, driven primarily by net unrealized losses on the fixed income portfolio, offset by net investment income.

growth_thesis.basis: Buyback and capital figures stated in the MD&A, the earnings release and the cash flow statement; the condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Per-share value growth is supported by capital deployment and buybacks. Book value per share was $2,243 at September 30, 2026. White Mountains repurchased shares at 93% of that book value and has roughly $0.8 billion of undeployed capital. Continuation requires shares to trade below book value and cash to remain available.
quotes: at an average share price of $2,088.39, or 93% of White Mountains’s September 30, 2026 book value per share.
As of September 30, 2026, White Mountains’s undeployed capital is roughly $0.8 billion.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release and the 10-Q MD&A; the condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: HG Global's municipal bond reinsurance volume is growing, but its book value returns are weak. It wrote a record $19 million of gross written premiums in the quarter, yet higher interest rates produced investment losses and a lower fair value of the BAM Surplus Notes. Continuation requires BAM issuance volume and interest rates to cooperate.
quotes: HG Global generated a record $19 million of gross written premiums in the quarter, but book value returns were negatively impacted by higher interest rates.

material_events.claim: White Mountains agreed to sell 5.5 million MediaAlpha shares at $13.90 per share. The filing does not say the sale has closed.
quotes: On November 4, 2026, White Mountains agreed to sell 5.5 million shares of MediaAlpha for $13.90 per share.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited item; the purchase prices are not stated in the cited text
material_events.claim: WTM Partners made two acquisitions, Basesix and Hawkeye Electric, which helped drive its revenue and earnings growth.
quotes: The increases were driven by organic growth at Enterprise Solutions and the acquisitions of Basesix and Hawkeye Electric in the second quarter of 2026.

material_events.claim: White Mountains repurchased and retired 103,827 common shares for $217 million in the first nine months of 2026.
quotes: In the first nine months of 2026, White Mountains repurchased and retired 103,827 of its common shares for $217

material_events.claim: Ark recorded estimated losses from the Iran war of $10 million in the third quarter and $52 million in the first nine months of 2026, net of reinsurance and reinstatement premiums.
quotes: In the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, Ark recorded estimated losses of $10 million and $52 million (net of reinsurance and reinstatement premiums) related to the Iran war.

risks.basis: stated in P4 and P5; the mechanism is inferred from the statements' structure
risks.claim: Book value per share is exposed to mark-to-market swings in the investment portfolio. In Q3 2026 higher rates and a lower MediaAlpha price produced unrealized losses, and book value per share ended at $2,243, down 1% for the quarter. MediaAlpha alone cost $54 million of unrealized losses.
quotes: Results in the third quarter were impacted by higher interest rates and a decline in the MediaAlpha share price, which led to unrealized losses that offset an otherwise solid quarter for operating results.

risks.basis: stated in P4; the future impact is inferred
risks.claim: Ark carries ongoing loss exposure to the war in Iran, mainly through its specialty and marine & energy lines. It booked an estimated $52 million of losses on this in the first nine months of 2026.
quotes: Ark has ongoing exposure to the war in Iran, primarily through the specialty and marine & energy lines of business.

risks.basis: stated in P4; the earnings effect is inferred
risks.claim: Softening property market conditions are reducing Ark's writings. Nine-month gross written premiums were $2,254 million, against $2,289 million a year earlier.
quotes: The decrease in gross written premiums in the first nine months of 2026 was driven primarily by reduced writings in property as a result of the softening market conditions

risks.basis: pre-tax loss stated in P4; impairment mechanism stated generically in P2; link between the two inferred
risks.claim: Distinguished is loss-making at the pre-tax level, with a $41 million pre-tax loss for the first nine months of 2026. It carries acquisition goodwill and intangibles, so impairment is a risk the 10-K identifies in general terms.
quotes: If we are required to write down goodwill and other intangible assets, it could materially adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

risks.claim: HG Global's BAM Surplus Notes depend on regulatory approval for payment. They are valued with a discounted cash flow, and a $16 million fair-value decrease in Q3 2026 took them to $336 million.
quotes: No payment of principal or interest on the BAM Surplus Notes may be made without the approval of the NYDFS.

risks.basis: stated in P2 (generic risk factor); no 2026 carrier data in the packet
risks.claim: Distinguished depends on a few carriers: about 22% of its 2025 business was placed with its single largest carrier and about 61% with its three largest. A carrier cutting volume or commission rates would reduce its commission revenue.
quotes: Distinguished placed approximately 22% of its business with its single largest carrier during the year ended December 31, 2025.

risks.claim: A downgrade of Ark's financial strength rating would limit its ability to write business. The 10-K says an 'A-' or better rating is particularly important to Ark, and the rating was A/stable at December 2025.
quotes: The maintenance of an “A-” or better financial strength rating is particularly important to Ark’s ability to write property and casualty insurance and reinsurance business in most markets.

risks.basis: figures stated in F1, F3 and P4; the liquidity risk itself is inferred and speculative
risks.claim: Capital return and acquisitions have used cash and added debt: share repurchases were 216,800,000 in the nine months, and consolidated debt rose to 928,600,000 from 837,000,000.0 at year-end. Evidence of a liquidity squeeze is weak.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, White Mountains’s undeployed capital is roughly $0.8 billion.

unresolved_questions.basis: The balance and buyback figures are stated in P4 and F3. The question about intended use is inferred from the absence of any stated plan.
unresolved_questions.claim: How and when will the roughly $0.8 billion of undeployed capital be used, as against further share repurchases? Nine-month buybacks were already large.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, White Mountains’s undeployed capital is roughly $0.8 billion.

unresolved_questions.basis: Losses and EBITDA are stated in P4. The goodwill-support concern is inferred, because the balance sheet carries goodwill and other intangibles for the segment and no impairment testing result is given.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will Distinguished move from pre-tax losses to profit, and does its large goodwill and intangible balance stay supported? It reported pre-tax losses for the quarter and the nine months.
quotes: Distinguished reported managed premiums of $159 million and $480 million, commission and fee revenues of $55 million and $151 million, pre-tax loss of $13 million and $41 million and ScaleCo adjusted EBITDA of $5 million and $22 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026.

unresolved_questions.basis: The premium and ratio figures are stated in P4. Whether softening will erode margins is inferred and is not stated.
unresolved_questions.claim: Can Ark keep its low combined ratio and premium growth as property pricing softens? Nine-month gross written premiums fell while the third-quarter combined ratio was 75%.
quotes: The decrease in gross written premiums in the first nine months of 2026 was driven primarily by reduced writings in property as a result of the softening market conditions, partially offset by growth in the specialty, casualty and accident & health lines of business.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P4 that exposure is ongoing and $52 million has been recorded. The eventual size is not given and is unknown.
unresolved_questions.claim: How large will Ark's ultimate losses from the Iran war be? Exposure is described as ongoing, and estimates so far are for the third quarter and nine months.
quotes: Ark has ongoing exposure to the war in Iran, primarily through the specialty and marine & energy lines of business.

unresolved_questions.basis: The balances and charge are printed in F1 and F2. The mechanism is inferred from the earlier 10-K explanation, and the payment terms are not in the packet.
unresolved_questions.claim: What is the schedule and ultimate size of the Ark contingent consideration liability, which keeps rising and is charged to earnings? It is tied to Ark's growth.
quotes: Ark’s book value includes goodwill and other intangible assets, net of tax, and White Mountains’s contingent consideration liability, which are excluded from Ark’s tangible book value.

unresolved_questions.basis: Prices and share counts are stated in P4. Any resulting Q4 accounting effect is inferred and not stated.
unresolved_questions.claim: What gain or loss and cash proceeds will result from the agreed MediaAlpha share sale, relative to the September 30 carrying value, and will it complete as agreed? The sale was agreed after quarter-end.
quotes: On November 4, 2026, White Mountains agreed to sell 5.5 million shares of MediaAlpha for $13.90 per share.

unresolved_questions.basis: The decrease and its stated driver are in P4. Future sensitivity to other inputs and the likelihood of New York regulator approval of payments are not quantified here.
unresolved_questions.claim: How sensitive are the fair value of the BAM Surplus Notes and the HG Global results to interest rates? Higher rates reduced fair value this quarter.
quotes: The decrease in fair value was driven primarily by the impact of higher interest rates on the discount rate.

unresolved_questions.basis: The balance and cash flow figures are printed in F1 and F3. The open allocation question is inferred from the lack of a purchase price allocation in the packet.
unresolved_questions.claim: What do the WTM Partners acquisitions contribute, and how is the large rise in goodwill and intangibles being allocated? The 2026 purchases include Basesix and Hawkeye Electric.
quotes: The increases were driven by organic growth at Enterprise Solutions and the acquisitions of Basesix and Hawkeye Electric in the second quarter of 2026.
